sections.text_helper: Section 24.4.10 "OPAMP operational amplifier offset compensation" in chapter 24 (Operational amplifier (OPAMP)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 737.
sections.section_content:
The peripheral incorporates a trimming circuitry that impacts the operational amplifier input
offset. The trimming circuitry is controlled through the TRIMOFFSETN[4:0] (for the N
differential pair) and TRIMOFFSETP[4:0] (for the P differential pair) bitfields of the OPAMP
control/status register (OPAMP_CSR).
The TRIMOFFSETN[4:0] and TRIMOFFSETP[4:0] bitfields keep the trimming value for the
N differential pair and P differential pair, respectively.
Upon reset, these registers are loaded with factory trimming values stored in the nonvolatile
memory. As the USERTRIM bit is low, the TRIMOFFSETN[4:0] and TRIMOFFSETP[4:0]
control bitfields are read-only.
Note: The factory trimming values result from a calibration procedure run on the production line in
specific production conditions.
When the offset compensation obtained with the factory trimming values is not acceptable
for a specific use case (supply voltage, operating temperature), the user software can apply
different trimming values.
To modify the trimming values, the user software has first to set the USERTRIM bit to allow
writing into the TRIMOFFSETN[4:0] and TRIMOFFSETP[4:0] control bitfields.
To retain the user trimming values, the user software has to write them into a nonvolatile
memory. It typically retrieves them from the nonvolatile memory and writes into
TRIMOFFSETN[4:0] and TRIMOFFSETP[4:0] at the startup, before the first use of OPAMP.
The resolution of the offset trimming allows reducing the input offset voltage to a value
defined in the datasheet, at a defined supply voltage and die temperature.
